scope: R3 / UNINST-01 item 347: identify files that would block deletion before any deletion runs, instead of discovering the lock only after the attempt fails
status: implemented-and-isolated-verified; no real user environment touched
gapClosed: The preview counted files and reparse points but never asked whether a file was in use. A locked file surfaced only as a partial failure after `execute_uninstall_scope` had already detached the current junction, leaving the user with a half-applied delete and no warning.

implementation.probe: file_blocks_deletion opens each file with DELETE access and closes immediately. Nothing is modified: requesting DELETE answers 'would deleting this fail right now'.
implementation.errorDiscrimination: Only ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION (32) counts as in use. Access-denied is a permissions problem and must never be reported as a lock.
implementation.boundedSampling: The preview probes at most LOCK_PROBE_LIMIT (200) files and the text says whether it checked everything ('已检查全部 N 个文件') or only a sample ('已抽样检查前 N 个文件（共 M 个）'). An empty tree says no check was needed.
implementation.reporting: Locks land in `unverified` under the resource name 文件占用 with the affected relative paths (first 10 listed, remainder counted) and an instruction to close the owning program. A lock does not block the preview: the scope stays complete so the user can decide with full information.

defectFoundAndFixed.symptom: Existing fixture `uninstall_reports_partial_failure_when_a_managed_file_is_locked` started failing with 卸载预览已变化，请重新生成预览后再执行.
defectFoundAndFixed.cause: validate_uninstall_execution_preview compares the whole UninstallPreview for equality. Lock state is an observation about the environment, not part of the deletion scope, so a file opened between preview and execution made a valid preview look changed.
defectFoundAndFixed.fix: Both sides now drop the LOCK_RESOURCE entries before comparing. The preview still reports locks to the user; only the scope-equality check ignores them.
defectFoundAndFixed.whyItMatters: Without this, any program opening a file during the confirmation dialog would force the user to re-preview, and the new feature would have broken the pre-existing partial-failure path.

notVerified: No real running program was used to hold a real environment file; the lock is a fixture handle with share_mode(0)
Only file locks are probed. A directory held open by a process, or a mapped executable image, is not covered
The 200-file limit means a large environment is only sampled; the text says so but the user cannot raise the limit
limitations: Item 347 also asks to identify the current environment and PATH references before deletion, and to detect related processes; only the file-lock part is implemented
Process identification is not attempted: mapping a handle back to a process needs elevated APIs this app does not use
The probe adds one open/close per sampled file to preview latency; not measured on a large environment
UI shows the entry through the existing 未验证 scope list, without a dedicated lock icon
